blocks.text: A circuit breaker temporarily stops calls to a dependency that is failing or responding too slowly.
It helps prevent repeated failed calls from consuming resources and spreading failures to other services.
Closed: calls pass through, and the breaker tracks failures or slow calls.
Open: after a configured threshold is reached, calls fail immediately without reaching the dependency.
Half-open: after a waiting period, a limited number of trial calls check recovery. Success closes the breaker; further failures reopen it.
If a payment service repeatedly times out, the checkout service opens its circuit breaker and reports that payment is temporarily unavailable.
Timeouts still bound individual calls. A circuit breaker does not repair the dependency or guarantee that a fallback is safe.
